title: STORY-009 Data Freshness Monitoring: evidence
summary: STORY-009 works on the demo deployment, with synthetic data; it is not operating in production. Every profile save, eligibility check, application, case status change and assignment is timed from the start of the write until a separate read sees the new row version, the way the next request would. Staff get a Data Freshness page with p50, p95 and p99 per data type against a 30-second target for 95% of updates, an alert when a type falls behind, the slowest updates split into write time and wait time, and a Check now button that times a write end to end from the browser.

Screens 1 to 3 come from an automated run against a local copy of the deployed code, seeded through the API, because the demo site has no test case-manager accounts. Screen 3 follows a real slowdown: the run held one applicant's database row locked for 31 seconds while that applicant saved a profile. Screens 4 and 5 are the deployed demo site.
checks: Demo deployment (scripts/verify-deploy.mjs): the API and the site serve 36a98bd; all 8 page paths serve the current build; database ok; 14 migrations applied; all 22 protected GET routes answer 401 without a token.
On the demo deployment, signed in as a synthetic citizen (scripts/verify-live-citizen.mjs): all 13 staff GET routes answer 403, no staff links show, and the freshness page refuses the citizen.
UI run (scripts/evidence/story-009.mjs): 8 checks passed, including the alert after the 31-second slowdown.
API end to end, local (scripts/e2e): 105 checks passed: access 33, case workflow 26, compliance 30, freshness 16.
Unit tests: 150 passed, including 12 new freshness tests and 117 route-access checks across all 40 routes.

shots.title: On target
shots.caption: Sam Ortiz, a case manager, opens Data Freshness after ordinary activity: 19 updates across four data types, all readable within 30 seconds, p95 172 ms. Each type shows when it last changed and how long its changes take.

shots.title: Check now, end to end
shots.caption: Check now writes a record and times how long until a separate read sees it: readable 27 ms after the write began on the server. The browser's round trip was 50 ms, so about 23 ms was network and request handling.

shots.title: A real slowdown raises the alert
shots.caption: One applicant's database row was held locked for 31 seconds while that applicant saved a profile. Profile updates' p95 rose to 31.1 s, over the 30 s target, and the page raised the alert; the slowest-updates list shows the time went into the write, not the wait to read. Every other data type stayed in milliseconds.

shots.title: Demo site: a citizen's dashboard
shots.caption: The deployed demo site lists data freshness as done in the release progress, and a citizen sees no staff links.

shots.title: Demo site: a citizen opening /freshness
shots.caption: The page refuses, and the demo site's API answers 403 to a citizen on all 13 staff routes.

notes: Measured on the demo deployment, which reads straight from its database with no cache or read replica yet, so a change is readable as soon as it is written. The same check, reading the row version on a separate request, will measure cache or replica lag when those arrive with AWS.

CloudWatch metrics, named in the story's acceptance criteria, need the AWS environment (STORY-004, waiting on approval). Until then the same figures come from the demo's own measurements. Cache miss rate does not apply yet because the demo has no cache.

Removed in this story: the /api/data and /api/latency placeholder endpoints. One reported data as fresh without measuring anything; another, a staff-only cleanup endpoint, put a request value straight into SQL. The route table now holds 40 routes.

After a deploy, the site's CDN can serve the previous page for a deep link for up to 5 minutes. verify-deploy now waits until all page paths serve the current build before reporting a deploy as verified.
